correctness.rationale: The Fourier core eigenvalues are 0, +sqrt(3), -sqrt(3) in the stated gauge. Squaring each traceless shifted 2x2 sector gives (lambda^2+4)I/4. Exponentiation and summation with Fourier projector entries exp(2pi i s(k-j)/3)/3 give the stated cosine phase and kernel. The triangle bound yields amplitude (1+4/sqrt(7))/3. Independent sign flips in Q(sqrt(3),sqrt(7)) prove frequency independence, so the continuous torus orbit and every positive-time tail are dense; for each pair the two sines and shifted cosine can approach +1. Equality would require both sine magnitudes to be 1 and hence a rational ratio of their frequencies, impossible. The probability constant, its digits as written, and all nine singleton-pair quantifiers are correct. Independent direct matrix power series checked 36 amplitudes with maximum discrepancy 2.7e-14; this corroborates the kernel, not the infinite-time conclusion.
residual_risks: Only the fixed Hamiltonian and single-site probabilities are verified; no waiting-time bound or optimization over parameters is asserted.

evidence: For m=1 the cross-block entries of the two projectors per core eigenvalue mu have opposite weights +1/sqrt(mu^2+4) and -1/sqrt(mu^2+4) times the core projector entry. value.rationale: The channel is motivated by the router's asymmetric performance, and the number is useful as a benchmark. However the contribution as a narrow exact invariant is a mechanical evaluation of the already solved six-site spectral model using its already established frequency basis; it offers no further structural or performance result beyond those inputs. The benchmark does not meet the bar for an independently valuable new exact invariant.
residual_risks: A different problem such as quantifying waiting times would require a separate claim and audit; none is established in the frozen record.
